question: Two beans of type PaymentClient exist; one is marked @Primary and the injection point uses @Qualifier("backupClient"). Which bean is injected?
explanation: An explicit @Qualifier at the injection point takes precedence over @Primary.

question: How can a bean receive every bean that implements a NotificationSender interface?
options: Inject the ApplicationContext and call getBean(NotificationSender.class)
explanation: Spring injects all matching beans into a collection-typed injection point, ordered by @Order or Ordered when present.

question: What does placing @Lazy on a constructor parameter do?
options: Delays the whole application startup until first request
Skips injection if the bean is missing
Injects a proxy that resolves the real bean on first use
explanation: @Lazy at an injection point injects a lazy-resolution proxy, which also helps break circular dependencies.

question: What is ObjectProvider<T> useful for at an injection point?
options: Lazily or optionally obtaining a bean, e.g. with getIfAvailable()
Registering new bean definitions at runtime
Converting a bean into a different type
Forcing a singleton to become a prototype
explanation: ObjectProvider allows deferred, optional or unique-if-available retrieval without failing at startup.

question: In Spring Boot 3, where are auto-configuration classes registered in a library jar?
explanation: Boot 3 removed support for registering auto-configurations in spring.factories; the AutoConfiguration.imports file is used instead.

question: What does @ConditionalOnMissingBean on an auto-configured @Bean method achieve?
options: The bean is created only if no other configuration class exists
The bean is created lazily on first injection
The default bean backs off if the application already defines a bean of that type
The bean replaces any user-defined bean of that type
explanation: This is how auto-configuration lets user-defined beans override Boot's defaults.

question: When does an auto-configuration annotated with @ConditionalOnClass(DataSource.class) apply?
options: Only when a DataSource bean is already defined
Only when the class is annotated with @Entity
Only when DataSource is present on the classpath
explanation: @ConditionalOnClass checks classpath presence, which is how starters trigger configuration just by being added.

question: Which annotation, introduced in Spring Boot 2.7, marks a class as an auto-configuration?
explanation: @AutoConfiguration is a specialized @Configuration with proxyBeanMethods=false and before/after ordering attributes.

question: How do you handle exceptions globally for all REST controllers?
options: A try-catch block in the main method
An @ExceptionHandler on the main application class
explanation: @RestControllerAdvice applies @ExceptionHandler methods across controllers and writes their results as response bodies.

question: Which Spring Framework 6 class represents an RFC 7807 problem details error response?
explanation: ProblemDetail models the standard type, title, status, detail and instance fields of a problem details response.

question: A @Valid @RequestBody fails Bean Validation in a Spring MVC controller. What happens by default?
options: The invalid fields are silently set to null
The request is retried without validation
MethodArgumentNotValidException is thrown, resulting in a 400 response
explanation: Spring MVC raises MethodArgumentNotValidException, which default exception handling maps to 400 Bad Request.

question: Which fluent synchronous HTTP client was introduced in Spring Framework 6.1 as a modern alternative to RestTemplate?
explanation: RestClient offers a fluent API over the same infrastructure as RestTemplate; WebClient is the reactive client.

question: What does nativeQuery = true on a Spring Data @Query annotation mean?
options: The query runs outside any transaction
The query string is plain SQL instead of JPQL
The query is compiled at startup into a stored procedure
The results are returned as raw JDBC ResultSet objects
explanation: With nativeQuery = true the string is sent to the database as SQL rather than parsed as JPQL.

question: Which annotation must accompany a @Query that performs an UPDATE or DELETE in Spring Data JPA?
explanation: @Modifying tells Spring Data to execute the query as an update via executeUpdate instead of expecting a result set.

question: Which is a standard way to avoid the N+1 select problem when loading orders with their items?
options: Switch the association to FetchType.EAGER everywhere
Call findAll() twice to warm the cache
Use a JOIN FETCH query or an @EntityGraph
explanation: Fetch joins and entity graphs load the association in the same query instead of one query per parent.

question: What is Spring Boot's default for spring.jpa.open-in-view?
options: true, and Boot logs a warning when it is not set explicitly
false, so lazy loading fails in views by default
It is undefined until a profile sets it
true only when the prod profile is active
explanation: Open Session in View is enabled by default, and Boot warns because it keeps a database connection open during view rendering.

question: In Spring Security 6, which DSL configures URL authorization rules?
explanation: antMatchers and mvcMatchers were removed in Spring Security 6; requestMatchers inside authorizeHttpRequests is the replacement.

question: Which authority does hasRole("ADMIN") check for?
explanation: hasRole adds the ROLE_ prefix automatically, whereas hasAuthority compares the exact string.

question: Which annotation enables @PreAuthorize support in Spring Security 6?
explanation: @EnableMethodSecurity replaces the deprecated @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity and enables pre/post annotations by default.

question: Why is CSRF protection often disabled for stateless REST APIs that use bearer tokens in the Authorization header?
options: Browsers do not attach such headers automatically, so cross-site forged requests cannot carry the token
Bearer tokens are encrypted with the CSRF token
CSRF only applies to GET requests
Spring Security cannot combine CSRF with JSON bodies
explanation: CSRF exploits credentials that browsers send automatically, such as cookies; a manually added header is not sent cross-site.

question: Which key format does Spring Boot recommend for properties in .properties and .yml files?
options: Dotted lowercase without separators, e.g. app.maxretrycount
explanation: Kebab-case is the canonical form; upper snake case is intended for environment variables.

question: Which environment variable overrides spring.datasource.url?
explanation: Relaxed binding maps environment variables by replacing dots with underscores, removing dashes and upper-casing.

question: What is spring.config.import used for?
options: Copying properties into the generated jar
Importing additional configuration sources, such as optional:file:./secrets.properties
explanation: spring.config.import pulls extra config data, and the optional: prefix avoids failure if the source is absent.

question: In Spring Boot 3, what is required to bind @ConfigurationProperties to a Java record with one constructor?
options: Nothing extra; constructor binding is used implicitly
explanation: Boot 3 infers constructor binding for a single constructor; @ConstructorBinding is only needed to choose among several.

question: In Spring Boot 3.4+, which Spring Framework annotation replaces the deprecated @MockBean?
explanation: Spring Framework 6.2 introduced @MockitoBean and @MockitoSpyBean, and Boot 3.4 deprecated @MockBean and @SpyBean.

question: What does @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT) do?
options: Uses a mock servlet environment with no server
Starts the server on port 8080 every time
Starts the real embedded server on a random free port
explanation: RANDOM_PORT starts a real server; the chosen port can be injected with @LocalServerPort.

question: What is @DynamicPropertySource typically used for in integration tests?
options: Marking a test as dependent on an external profile
Registering properties computed at runtime, such as a Testcontainers JDBC URL
explanation: The static method adds property suppliers to the Environment before the context starts.

question: What does @ServiceConnection on a Testcontainers container field do in Spring Boot 3.1+?
options: Auto-configures connection details for the app from the running container
Starts the container only when the prod profile is active
Mocks the external service without Docker
Registers the container as a Spring MVC endpoint
explanation: Boot derives ConnectionDetails beans from the container, removing the need for manual property wiring.

question: Which property exposes the health, info and metrics endpoints over HTTP?
explanation: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include lists the endpoints to expose over the web.

question: How do you add a custom check to /actuator/health?
explanation: Each HealthIndicator bean contributes a component that is aggregated into the overall health status.

question: What is needed for Actuator to serve a /actuator/prometheus scrape endpoint?
options: A Prometheus server embedded in the jar
Spring Cloud Sleuth on the classpath
The micrometer-registry-prometheus dependency plus exposing the endpoint
explanation: Boot auto-configures the Prometheus registry and endpoint when the Micrometer Prometheus registry is present.

question: Which health group paths does Spring Boot provide for Kubernetes probes?
explanation: Liveness and readiness groups are enabled automatically on Kubernetes and can be turned on elsewhere via management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled.

question: How do you make a @Transactional method roll back on a checked IOException?
options: Declare the exception with throws only
explanation: rollbackFor extends the default rule so specified checked exceptions also trigger rollback.

question: With default proxy-based Spring AOP, what happens to @Transactional on a private method?
options: A transaction is started via reflection
It is ignored and no transaction is started
The method becomes public at runtime
explanation: Proxies cannot intercept private methods, so the annotation has no effect.

question: What does Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW do when a transaction is already active?
options: Suspends the current transaction and starts an independent new one
explanation: The new transaction commits or rolls back independently, after which the outer one resumes.

question: Which class supports programmatic transaction demarcation with a callback?
explanation: TransactionTemplate.execute runs a callback inside a transaction using the configured PlatformTransactionManager.

question: Why do Spring Boot layered jars help when building Docker images?
options: They compress the jar to half its size
Dependencies and application classes go in separate layers, so unchanged layers are cached
They remove the need for a JVM in the image
They encrypt application classes inside the image
explanation: Rarely changing dependencies end up in lower layers, so rebuilding after a code change only replaces the application layer.

question: Which property configures graceful shutdown of the embedded web server?
explanation: With graceful shutdown the server stops accepting requests and waits for active ones, bounded by spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase.

question: Which Spring Boot 3 capability uses AOT processing to compile an app into a standalone native executable?
explanation: Boot 3 performs ahead-of-time processing so GraalVM can build a native executable with fast startup.

question: What must a Spring Boot app do to be deployed as a WAR to an external Tomcat?
options: Extend SpringBootServletInitializer and use war packaging with the Tomcat starter set to provided
Remove the main method and add web.xml only
explanation: SpringBootServletInitializer bootstraps the application when the servlet container starts the WAR.
